references.text: God identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the same formulation used in verse 15.
God establishes his eternal covenant with Abraham, pointing to 'this is my name forever'.
The LORD, your name endures forever; the LORD, your memorial from generation to generation - a direct parallel to 'זֶה־שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם וְזֶה זִכְרִי לְדֹר דֹּר'.
God's name shall endure forever, and his memorial from generation to generation.
The LORD is his name - confirming God's eternal name revealed at the burning bush.
I am the LORD; this is my name - God confirms his unique name.
Jesus quotes this text: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' to prove the resurrection.
Jesus refers to the burning bush and quotes 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'.
Jesus quotes Moses at the burning bush that the Lord is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Peter uses the expression 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers' in his speech.
Stephen quotes this verse in his speech: 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob'.
God is not ashamed to be called their God - a reference to the God of the patriarchs.
The identical name formula links God's eternal identity (3:15) directly to the requirement that the people believe in his revelation (4:5).
Ezekiel confirms and reflects on the same covenantal identity and God's revelation in Egypt as defined in Exodus 3:15.
God's identity as the God of the fathers (3:15) is the theological basis for the oaths concerning the land mentioned in 33:1.
